title: A Day at the Bakery
text: Lucia gets up at four every morning, long before the city begins to stir. By the time the first customers arrive, she has shaped about two hundred loaves and checked the ovens. Although the work is exhausting, she says it has taught her patience, because bread cannot be hurried. At midday she locks the door, eats a simple lunch, and sleeps for two hours. In the afternoon she answers orders, most of which are sent by restaurants that depend on her. Her sister has often suggested that she hire an assistant, but Lucia insists that she would rather do everything herself. She admits, however, that she may change her mind if the business keeps growing.

title: A Night Train North
text: Last spring Tomas decided to travel to the far north by train instead of flying. The journey, which lasted nearly two days, took him through forests so dense that the sunlight seldom reached the ground. He had been warned that the carriages would be cold, so he brought a thick blanket and a flask of tea. On the second evening a retired teacher sat opposite him and began telling stories about the villages they passed. Tomas later said that these conversations were the most valuable part of the trip. When the train finally pulled into the station, snow was falling softly on the empty platform. Although he arrived tired, he felt that the slow route had been worth the extra time.

title: A Message to the Landlord
text: Dear Samuel, I am writing about the heating in my flat, which has not worked since last Monday. A technician was supposed to visit on Thursday, but nobody came and nobody called to explain. Since the temperature at night has dropped below freezing, my neighbour and I have been using electric heaters. I would be grateful if you could arrange a repair as soon as possible. Should the problem continue, I will have to ask for a reduction in rent. I appreciate that these things take time, and I do not wish to cause difficulty. Please let me know by Friday when someone will be able to come. Thank you for your help, Amira.

title: A Community Garden Notice
text: The neighbourhood council is pleased to announce that the old car park behind the library will be turned into a community garden. Residents who wish to take part are invited to a meeting on the first Saturday of next month. Each household will be given a small plot, provided that it agrees to look after it throughout the growing season. Tools and seeds will be supplied free of charge, although volunteers are asked to bring their own gloves. Those who have no experience need not worry, since a team of experienced gardeners will offer guidance every weekend. It is hoped that the project will bring neighbours closer together and make the area greener. Anyone who is interested should sign the list at the library desk before the end of the week.

title: The Missing Keys
text: Elena had spent the whole afternoon searching for her car keys, turning the flat upside down. She checked every pocket, lifted every cushion, and even emptied the bin, but there was no sign of them. Convinced that someone must have taken them, she began to suspect her new flatmate, who had been strangely quiet all week. Eventually, close to tears, she phoned her mother to complain. Her mother listened patiently and then asked whether Elena was by any chance holding something in her left hand. Elena looked down and discovered that the keys had been in her hand the entire time. She laughed so hard that she had to sit down, and she later apologised to her flatmate with a cake.

title: The Old Harbour Town
text: The harbour town lies at the end of a narrow valley, where a river meets the sea. Its houses, painted in faded blue and yellow, climb the hillside in uneven rows. Visitors are often struck by the silence, which is broken only by the cry of gulls and the creak of fishing boats. In the main square stands a stone fountain that, according to local legend, has never run dry. Most of the shops are small and family owned, and many have remained unchanged for generations. Because the road is steep and winding, few tourists venture further than the first cafe. Those who do are rewarded with a view of the whole bay at sunset.

title: A Library Opens Late
text: A public library in a northern city has begun to stay open until midnight, following a request from local students. The scheme, which started last month, was introduced after a survey showed that many young people had nowhere quiet to study in the evenings. Officials report that the extra hours have been far more popular than expected, with every desk occupied on most nights. Some residents, however, have complained about the cost of keeping the building heated and staffed so late. The city council has replied that the project will be reviewed after six months. title: Why Handwriting Still Matters
text: Many people argue that handwriting is a skill we can safely abandon now that nearly everyone owns a keyboard. I believe this view is mistaken, or at least premature. Studies suggest that students who take notes by hand tend to remember more, because they are forced to summarise rather than copy. Writing slowly also gives the mind time to organise ideas before they reach the page. Of course, typing is faster, and nobody would deny that it is more practical for long documents. Nevertheless, speed is not the only measure of value. For that reason, I think schools should continue to teach handwriting, even if it occupies a smaller place in the timetable than before.

title: How a Heat Pump Works
text: A heat pump warms a house by moving heat rather than creating it. Even on a cold day, the air outside contains some warmth, which a liquid inside the machine absorbs and turns into gas. This gas is then compressed, and compression makes it much hotter, just as a bicycle pump becomes warm when it is used. The hot gas passes through a coil inside the house, where it gives up its heat and turns back into liquid. The cycle then begins again, repeating itself for as long as the machine is switched on. Because it transfers heat instead of burning fuel, a heat pump can deliver several times more energy than it consumes. This efficiency explains why such machines are becoming popular in countries with cold winters.

title: My Grandfather's Workshop
text: When I was about ten, I spent every summer holiday in my grandfather's workshop at the edge of the village. It smelled of sawdust and oil, and the walls were covered with tools that I was not allowed to touch. He rarely spoke while he worked, but he would occasionally hand me a piece of wood and tell me to feel the grain. At the time I found this boring, and I would have preferred to be playing outside with my cousins. Only years later did I understand that he had been teaching me to pay attention. He died shortly before I finished school, and the workshop was sold soon afterwards. Even now, the smell of fresh sawdust brings back those long quiet afternoons so vividly that I have to stop for a moment.
